hints.title: Pair Comparison Quadratic Obstacle
hints.text: Comparing every pair (i, j) requires O(N^2) comparisons. Which candidate left indices i are actually worth keeping when considering potential ramp starts?

hints.title: Strictly Decreasing Left Prefix Invariant
hints.text: An index i cannot be an optimal ramp start if there exists i0 < i with nums[i0] <= nums[i]. Thus, only strictly decreasing left indices need to be recorded.

hints.title: Prefix Building and Reverse Scan Procedure
hints.text: Build a list of strictly decreasing indices from left to right. Then iterate j from n - 1 down to 0: while the index list is non-empty and nums[j] >= nums[list[-1]], pop index i, record max width max(max_width, j - i). Return max_width.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of array nums (2 <= N <= 5 * 10^4)
complexity.notes: Building decreasing prefix indices and backward scanning each element at most once.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Examining all pairs (i, j) with i < j takes O(N^2) comparisons, timing out for N = 50,000.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Storing the strictly decreasing prefix indices takes O(N) auxiliary space but yields strictly O(N) runtime.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Recognizing that popping from the monotonic prefix during the reverse pass is safe because j decreases.
